standard.title: Managing health risk situations
standard.description: plan, rehearse and evaluate strategies for managing situations where their own or others' health, safety or wellbeing may be at risk
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan and implement strategies using health resources to enhance health, safety and wellbeing (AC9HP8P10). At Y9-10 the focus moves to more complex risk situations — peer pressure around substance use, first aid including CPR, consent under impairment, and safe blood practices — with evaluation of strategies added to planning and rehearsal.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, rehearse and evaluate strategies for managing health and safety risk situations, including peer pressure, first aid emergencies, digital safety, and safe practices in a range of risk contexts.

nodes.label: Identifying and planning for risk situations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify health risk situations and plan realistic strategies for managing them
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one health risk situation (e.g. peer pressure, emergency, digital safety risk) and plan a realistic response strategy
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of health risk situations relevant to young people; plan realistic responses including refusal skills, communicating choices, contingency plans; critique the appropriateness and effectiveness of support services available in the local community for young people
wider: Plan responses to scenarios involving peer pressure around e-cigarettes, cannabis, psychostimulants, opiates or hallucinogens — evaluate which refusal strategies are most realistic in peer group social contexts

Investigate safe blood practices across a range of situations (not sharing needles, precautions in physical activity, safe sexual practices including use of condoms and dams) and plan how to raise these practices with peers in an accessible way

Examine factors that impact ability to seek, give or deny consent when a person is affected by alcohol or other drugs, or where there is a power imbalance — plan strategies for recognising and responding to these situations
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot plan realistic strategies for named risk situations cannot rehearse and evaluate them in Node 2 — rehearsal requires a concrete plan to enact and evaluate.

response_modes.reason: Health risk situations are diverse — peer pressure around substances, physical emergencies, digital safety, and consent under impairment each require different strategies. Students need to plan across multiple risk types rather than developing one polished response. The elaborations explicitly require multiple risk contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Substance-specific peer pressure, safe blood practices, and consent-under-impairment planning each add a distinct risk context with its own strategic requirements. Students who plan across these wider contexts develop genuinely transferable risk management capability rather than competence with a single scenario type.
success_criteria: Names a specific health risk situation and identifies who may be at risk
Plans a realistic response strategy — not an idealised one that ignores social or contextual constraints
Plan includes at least one external resource or support service that could be accessed

nodes.label: Rehearsing and evaluating risk responses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can rehearse and evaluate strategies for managing health risk situations, including first aid responses
nodes.minimum_width: Rehearse one strategy for a health risk situation and evaluate its effectiveness — what worked, what barriers emerged, what would be done differently
nodes.typical_width: Rehearse responses to a range of risk scenarios including peer pressure situations and first aid emergencies (including CPR); evaluate the appropriateness and effectiveness of responses; investigate behaviours that constitute safe, legal and ethical conduct in digital environments and identify actions to take when behaviour becomes abusive
wider: Practise and evaluate CPR and basic first aid responses — evaluate own performance against criteria and identify what further practice is needed
Rehearse a range of realistic refusal skill scenarios (substance offers, unsafe situations) and evaluate which verbal and non-verbal strategies are most effective across different social contexts
Evaluate available digital safety resources and support services for young people — assess which are most accessible and effective for specific risk situations young people in your community face

response_modes.reason: Rehearsal across multiple risk scenario types builds a repertoire of response strategies that can be accessed in real situations. A single rehearsed response is insufficient — the elaborations explicitly require rehearsal across peer pressure scenarios, first aid emergencies, and digital safety situations. The evaluation component requires students to assess effectiveness, not just complete the rehearsal.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: CPR rehearsal with self-evaluation, range of refusal skill scenarios, and digital safety resource evaluation each add a distinct rehearsal and evaluation context. Students who engage these wider directions develop confidence and capability across a meaningfully broader range of real risk situations.
success_criteria: Rehearses a strategy for at least one named risk situation
Evaluates its effectiveness — identifies what worked, what was difficult, and what would be changed
Evaluation is specific to the scenario context, not generic ('it went well')
